text: Long ago, Suta maharshi spoke thus to Saunaka and the munis: O saints!
Parama Siva himself told Parvati devi of a vratham that showers soubhagya — prosperity — upon women.
For the benefit of the world I shall tell you of that vratham.
Hear it carefully.

One day, as Parameswara sat on his simhasana, Parvathi devi approached him and asked: "O swami, tell me of a vratham by which women gain every comfort, flourish through children and grandchildren, and attain moksha."
Siva replied: "O Devi!
There is one vratham that gives women all prosperity — it is the Varalakshmi vratam."
It should be performed, he said, on the Friday that comes before the pournami — the full-moon day — of Sravana masam.
Then Parvathi devi asked: "Deva!
Who first performed this Varalakshmi vratham?
Tell me in detail how it is to be done."
"Katyayani!
Once, in the land of Magadha, there was a city named Kundina nagaram.
In that city lived a woman named Charumathi — virtuous, obedient and patient.
She rose early every day, served her husband and her in-laws, and lived in friendship with her neighbours."
One night, Varalakshmi devi appeared in Charumathi's dream.
"Charumathi!
Worship me on the Friday before the full moon of Sravana masam, and I shall grant the boons and gifts you ask," she said, and disappeared.
Charumathi rejoiced: "O Mother!
Blessed are those who receive your grace — they live honoured, prosperous and learned.
O Pavani!
By the merit of my past lives I have been given your darshanam."
Thus she praised Lakshmi in many ways.
Waking, Charumathi knew it for a dream, and told it to her husband and her in-laws.
Overjoyed, they encouraged her to perform the Varalakshmi vratam.
The women of the city, hearing of her dream, also began waiting for that auspicious Friday before the pournami.
On that Sravana Friday, all the women of the city rose at dawn, bathed, dressed in silk, and gathered at Charumathi's house.

Charumathi arranged a mandapam in her home, poured rice upon it and set the kalasam on top, invited Varalakshmi devi into the kalasam with sankalpam, and worshipped her with the sixteen upacharas, offering naivedyams.
They tied the thoram — the sacred thread of nine strands — to their hands, and offered pradakshina namaskarams to Varalakshmi devi.
As they completed the first pradakshina, anklets rang out on their feet.
At the second, their hands shone with gem-studded golden bangles.
At the third, every one of them stood adorned in full ornament.
By the fruit of that Varalakshmi vratam, Charumathi's home — and the homes of all the women of that city — filled with wealth, gold and every good thing.

Chariots with elephants and horses came from their own houses to carry them home, and all along the way they praised Charumathi: the devi had appeared in her dream, and by her vratam she had made them all greatly fortunate.
Every year thereafter they performed the Varalakshmi vratam, lived in prosperity and happiness, and attained mukti.
O munis — this is the vratham that Paramasiva taught Parvati.
By hearing this story, by performing this vratham, or even by watching it performed, one gains all wealth, health, fortune and prosperity — so said Suta maha muni to Saunaka and the maharshis.
After hearing this story, place a few akshatas at Lakshmi devi's feet and a few upon your head.
Then give thamboolams to the muthaidhuvulu, distribute theertham and prasadam to all — and those who performed the puja should take them too.
This vratham may be done by anyone, of any community or tradition.
Pray with bhakthi, and mother Varalakshmi devi surely blesses you.
